import ThemePreview from '../../../components/themes/ThemePreview.astro';
import '@fontsource/roboto/400.css';
import '@fontsource/roboto/500.css';

```js
import '@fontsource/roboto/400.css';
import '@fontsource/roboto/500.css';
import '@argus-table/themes/material.css';
```

It borrows the feel of Material 3, not Google's exact spec: the baseline purple palette, Roboto, an outlined surface with 12px corners, a tinted header and deeper shadows on pinned columns.

- **Fonts:** the theme loads no fonts. Load Roboto 400 and 500 on the page, from [`@fontsource/roboto`](https://fontsource.org/fonts/roboto) as above or from Google Fonts. Without Roboto, the table uses the system font.
- **Rows:** taller than the table's defaults: 40, 52 and 60px for `compact`, `comfortable` (the default) and `spacious`, with 12, 16 and 20px of inline padding.
- **Light and dark:** `data-argus-theme="dark"` or `"light"` on the table or an ancestor forces a scheme; any token can be set after the theme. See [Themes](/argus-table/themes/).

The preview follows this site's light and dark switch. The status chips are the page's own CSS: cell content is light DOM.

<ThemePreview theme="material" label="Material-inspired theme" />
